cards.canonical_statement: For every real a and every positive real ε, there is a positive real δ such that |x-a|<δ implies |x-a|<ε for every real x.
cards.proof_strategy: Fix ε>0 and choose δ=ε; the two distance inequalities are identical.
sketch_steps: Fix arbitrary real a and positive real ε.
Choose δ=ε.
The choice is positive because ε>0.
Assume an arbitrary real x satisfies |x-a|<δ.
Substitute δ=ε to obtain |x-a|<ε and close the quantifiers.

cards.canonical_statement: For every real a, the derivative of x^2 at a is 2a.
cards.proof_strategy: Use the power rule for x² and normalize the resulting slope at a.
sketch_steps: Fix an arbitrary real a.
View x² as a polynomial real function.
Apply the derivative rule for the second power at a.
Simplify the coefficient to 2·a.
Record the result as HasDerivAt at the original point a.

cards.canonical_statement: For every real a, x^3 - 2x is differentiable at a.
cards.proof_strategy: Use differentiability closure for polynomial powers, scalar multiplication, and subtraction.
sketch_steps: Fix an arbitrary real a.
The map x↦x³ is differentiable at a.
The map x↦2x is differentiable at a.
Apply closure of differentiability under subtraction.
Conclude that x³-2x is differentiable at a.

cards.canonical_statement: The real function x ↦ x^2 is interval-integrable from 0 to 1.
cards.proof_strategy: Establish global continuity of x², then use continuity to obtain interval integrability.
sketch_steps: Recognize x↦x² as a polynomial real function.
Establish that this function is continuous on ℝ.
Restrict the continuity statement to the interval from 0 to 1.
Apply the continuity-implies-interval-integrable theorem for volume.
Conclude interval integrability on the oriented interval 0..1.

cards.lean_target: IntervalIntegrable (fun x : ℝ => x ^ 2) (MeasureTheory.volume : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ) 0 1
cards.lean_witness:
example : IntervalIntegrable (fun x : ℝ => x ^ 2)
    (MeasureTheory.volume : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ) 0 1 := by
  have hcont : Continuous (fun x : ℝ => x ^ 2) := by fun_prop
  exact hcont.intervalIntegrable (μ := (MeasureTheory.volume : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ)) 0 1
cards.alignment: realanalysis1:interval_integrable(f,a,b) lowers to IntervalIntegrable f volume a b. This admits the exact integration side condition, not an unsupported bare integral-value claim.
